task: STEP 1.5 -- phi Identity Stability Audit on Real Cross-Run Data (read-only analysis, no implementation)
head: 9f228723fad5406c72e62beca67ec70ea0fdb004

real_run_pairs.note: The two real runs already used in Step 1 (required minimum).
Additional healthy pair (semantic_execution_health PASS, classified_coverage 1.0 and 0.989 respectively), included as extra offline evidence per instruction.

current_phi_overlap.definition: Step 1's implemented granularity: whole per-(ticker, alpha_id) canonical edge SET must be byte-identical.
current_phi_overlap.conclusion: 0 of 14 checked alphas (across both ticker pairs) produced an identical whole-edge-set. Step 1's zero-phi-overlap finding is confirmed structural, not a one-off fluke of the two original NVDA runs.

node_overlap.conclusion: BY FAR the most stable granularity measured -- 77-85% of canonical factor nodes recur exactly across independent runs of the same ticker. Node identity (structure_extractor.py's existing id) is a strong, already-reusable lower-level primitive, but a bare node is a single factor's presence, not a causal RELATIONSHIP -- it carries no direction, no Alpha attribution, and no 'A causes B' information by itself.

edge_overlap.definition: Ticker-wide (NOT per-alpha) exact (source, edge_type, target) triples -- Candidate C2's core unit, without the alpha_id scope yet applied.

edge_type_variance_on_same_node_pair.conclusion: Ignoring edge_type and comparing (source, target) only raises overlap modestly (NVDA 6/15=0.40 vs typed 5/19=0.26; MSFT 3/14=0.21 vs typed 2/16=0.125) -- edge_type disagreement between independent extractions is a REAL but SECONDARY contributor to instability, not the dominant one.

edge_overlap.conclusion: Genuine recurring edges DO exist (5 of 19 union for NVDA, 2 of 16 for MSFT) -- individual edges are meaningfully more stable than whole per-alpha edge sets, though still far short of node-level stability.

two_edge_motif.definition: Deterministic 2-hop chains (edge1.target == edge2.source) among edges sharing one alpha_id.

three_edge_motif.definition: Deterministic 3-hop chains among edges sharing one alpha_id.

motif_overlap.conclusion: Multi-hop motifs are RARE even within a single run (most alphas produce zero 2- or 3-edge motifs at all -- their linked edges do not chain into a path), and where they do exist, cross-run overlap is ZERO in every case measured. Motif-level identity is empirically LESS stable than edge-level, not more -- moving to motifs would make the zero-overlap problem worse, not better.

component_overlap.definition: Per-alpha connected components (undirected) among that alpha's linked edges.

MSFT.all_alphas: 0 or 1 components per run, 0 exact overlap in every case

component_overlap.conclusion: No better than edge-level (1 exact match out of 14 alpha-component comparisons across both pairs) and structurally coarser/less specific -- a component can silently absorb an unrelated edge added anywhere in the same alpha's local subgraph. Not recommended as a standalone identity layer.

alpha_assignment_instability.finding: Even among the exact-identical (source, edge_type, target) edges that DO recur across runs, the SET of alpha_ids attached to that same literal edge sometimes differs between runs.
alpha_assignment_instability.conclusion: This is a SEPARATE and materially important root cause, distinct from edge content changing: the SAME literal causal claim can be linked to a different Alpha (or to no Alpha at all) by independent Alpha Mapper/LLM classification runs. This means Step 1's per-alpha SET requirement fails even in cases where the underlying edge content is byte-identical, purely because of alpha-attribution variance. An edge-level phi scoped by (ticker, alpha_id, edge) converts this from a silent all-or-nothing SET failure into an honest, partial, edge-by-edge picture: the edge matches under whichever alpha_id(s) both runs agree on, and simply does not match under an alpha_id only one run assigned -- without needing to invent any similarity threshold.

root_cause_of_zero_phi_overlap: Edge additions/removals between independent runs: different real-world claims get sampled/extracted each run (different day, different agent-report phrasing), so the raw edge inventory itself differs run to run -- confirmed by edge-level union counts (19 for NVDA, 16 for MSFT) being much larger than either run's own edge count alone.

edge_type disagreement on the same (source, target) node pair between independent LLM-driven canonical-relation extraction (e.g. ai_capex->gpu_demand classified causal in one run, supportive in another) -- a real, secondary contributor.

Alpha-attribution instability: the identical literal edge is sometimes linked to a different alpha_id set across runs (see alpha_assignment_instability above) -- a real, materially significant contributor, independent of edge content changing.

Structural consequence of requiring an entire SET match: Step 1's implementation demands perfect agreement across EVERY edge linked to an alpha simultaneously -- with typically only 1-5 edges per alpha, even a single one of the above three effects on any ONE edge is enough to break the whole-set match to exact zero. This amplifies small, individually-explainable differences into total non-recognition.

candidate_identity_models.name: Whole-Alpha edge set (current Step 1 implementation)
candidate_identity_models.stability: LOW (0 of 14 alpha-pairs matched across both real ticker pairs)
candidate_identity_models.semantic_specificity: HIGH (captures an alpha's full local structure at once)
candidate_identity_models.collision_risk: LOW (a full-set match is a very strong signal when it does occur)
candidate_identity_models.fragmentation_risk: VERY HIGH (any single edge/type/alpha-attribution difference anywhere in the set breaks the entire match)
candidate_identity_models.cross_run_usefulness: NONE observed on real data -- empirically fails to serve the Development Plan's 'match recurring causal chains' purpose.

candidate_identity_models.name: Single canonical edge phi (ticker + alpha_id + source + edge_type + target + version authority)
candidate_identity_models.stability: MODERATE (5/19 NVDA, 2/16 MSFT edges recur exactly at the ticker-wide level; per-alpha scoping narrows this further but converts all-or-nothing failure into partial, edge-by-edge recognition -- see alpha_assignment_instability)
candidate_identity_models.semantic_specificity: MODERATE (one causal relationship, not a full thesis, but a genuine directed causal/supportive/conflicting claim)
candidate_identity_models.fragmentation_risk: MODERATE (a genuinely-recurring chain still fragments into several independently-tracked edge phi ids rather than one atomic identity, but each piece is individually far more likely to be recognized than the whole)
candidate_identity_models.implementation_complexity: LOW (same hashing approach as C1, applied to individual edges instead of edge sets)
candidate_identity_models.cross_run_usefulness: DEMONSTRATED on real data -- concrete recurring edges were found and enumerated for both ticker pairs.

candidate_identity_models.name: Two-edge causal motif (A->B->C)
candidate_identity_models.stability: VERY LOW (0 of 4 alpha-pairs with any 2-edge motif at all shared a motif across runs; most alphas produce zero motifs even within one run)
candidate_identity_models.semantic_specificity: HIGH (a genuine mini-chain, closest to the Development Plan's own worked example)
candidate_identity_models.fragmentation_risk: VERY HIGH -- worse than C1, since it requires simultaneous agreement on two edges at once, compounding C2's own instability

candidate_identity_models.name: Maximal deterministic path
candidate_identity_models.stability: NOT EVALUATED AS UNAMBIGUOUS -- the real graphs' linked-edge subgraphs branch and span multiple components per alpha (see NVDA A101/A103's own 2/1 component counts), so 'the' maximal path is not deterministically defined without an arbitrary tie-break rule this audit refuses to invent, per the same Chain Boundary Rule documented in Step 1.
candidate_identity_models.implementation_complexity: HIGH (would require inventing a path-selection heuristic)
candidate_identity_models.cross_run_usefulness: NOT EVALUATED -- disqualified by ambiguity, consistent with the instruction to only implement path construction where graph topology makes it unambiguous.

candidate_identity_models.name: Connected component per alpha
candidate_identity_models.stability: LOW (1 of 14 alpha-pairs showed any exact component overlap)
candidate_identity_models.semantic_specificity: LOW-MODERATE (a whole local subgraph, not a specific claim)
candidate_identity_models.collision_risk: MODERATE (a component can absorb an unrelated edge added anywhere in the same local subgraph, diluting specificity)
candidate_identity_models.fragmentation_risk: HIGH (similar failure mode to C1 -- one added/removed edge changes the component's exact membership)
candidate_identity_models.cross_run_usefulness: MINIMAL observed on real data (1 match out of 14 comparisons).

candidate_identity_models.name: Hierarchical identity (phi_structure_id > phi_motif_id > phi_edge_id)
candidate_identity_models.stability: Inherits phi_edge_id's MODERATE stability as its most durable layer; phi_structure_id (C1-equivalent) remains the least stable, retained only as a coarse audit/display aggregate, never as the primary matching unit; the motif layer is NOT populated in v1 given C3's empirically zero cross-run usefulness today.
candidate_identity_models.semantic_specificity: Best of all candidates -- exposes both the atomic recurring fact (edge) AND the coarser per-alpha grouping (structure) simultaneously, each honestly labeled with its own stability profile.
candidate_identity_models.collision_risk: LOW at the edge layer (same as C2); the structure layer inherits C1's already-low collision risk.
candidate_identity_models.fragmentation_risk: LOW-MODERATE overall -- a fragmenting whole-structure match no longer discards the edges that DID genuinely recur; they remain individually visible at the phi_edge_id layer.
candidate_identity_models.implementation_complexity: MODERATE (two concurrently-exposed granularities instead of one; no motif layer needed initially, reducing scope versus a full 3-layer build)
candidate_identity_models.cross_run_usefulness: Combines C2's demonstrated real-data usefulness with C1's already-implemented coarse aggregate, without discarding either.

node_id_reuse_investigation.node_level_overlap_vs_edge_level: Node overlap (0.77-0.85 Jaccard) is roughly 3-6x higher than typed-edge overlap (0.125-0.263) and vastly higher than per-alpha edge-set overlap (0.0 in every case measured) -- node identity is materially, dramatically more stable than any relational granularity.
node_id_reuse_investigation.can_node_identity_safely_serve_as_a_lowe: YES, as an INPUT to edge/chain identity (which it already is, since an edge's source/target ARE node ids) -- but NOT as a standalone phi unit by itself, since a bare node carries no causal direction, no Alpha attribution, and no 'this is a claim about a relationship' semantics. It is necessary infrastructure, not sufficient identity.
node_id_reuse_investigation.does_the_revenue_growth_scoping_inconsis: NO practical effect in this audit's measurements: both ticker pairs' phi computations are already ticker-scoped at the TOP LEVEL (ticker is a first-class hashed field per Step 1's Product Decision 2), independent of whatever scoping a given node id itself uses. The inconsistency (only 'Revenue Growth' is ticker-scoped in the node id string; ~109 other factors share an identical node id string across ALL tickers) would only matter for a hypothetical future feature that compared node ids DIRECTLY across tickers without an explicit ticker field of its own -- which is exactly what Step 1 avoided by design. This audit's own analysis confirms that design choice was correct: e.g. NVDA and MSFT both contain a node literally named 'ai_capex' (ticker-independent, unscoped) -- without Step 1's explicit ticker hash field, these would incorrectly appear as 'the same structure' across two unrelated companies.
node_id_reuse_investigation.should_node_ids_change_in_this_step: NO -- not evaluated for change, and this audit found no evidence requiring one. Node ids remain the correct, stable, reusable lower-level primitive they already were found to be in the original Step 0 audit.

recommended_phi_model: E_HIERARCHICAL_PHI (edge-level as the atomic/durable layer, whole-alpha-structure retained only as a coarser, non-primary aggregate; motif layer explicitly NOT included in v2 given C3's measured zero cross-run usefulness)
recommendation_reasoning: Evidence rules out C1 (0% match rate, confirmed structural failure, not implementable-as-is for the Plan's stated purpose), C3/motifs (measured WORSE than C1 -- rarer within a single run and zero cross-run overlap in every case found), C4 (topologically ambiguous on real data, would require inventing a path rule), and C5/components (1 match in 14 comparisons, no better than edges while being less specific). C2 (single edge) is the only candidate with DEMONSTRATED real cross-run recurrence (5/19 and 2/16 exact edge matches with concrete examples). Recommending pure C2 alone, however, would discard the already-implemented and already-tested C1 aggregate for no reason -- C6/hierarchical keeps C1 as a coarse, honestly-labeled roll-up while promoting C2's edges to be the actual matching primitive. This is additive to Step 1's existing work, not a full rewrite: phi_identity.py's chain_edges computation and hashing approach are directly reusable, applied per-edge instead of per-set.

one_alpha_multiple_phi_tokens_answer.answer: YES -- one Alpha should be allowed to contain multiple persistent phi tokens (one per recurring edge it is linked to), not exactly one.
one_alpha_multiple_phi_tokens_answer.evidence: Every alpha examined in both real ticker pairs has 1-5 distinct linked edges, several of which independently recur across runs while others do not (see current_phi_overlap's per-alpha breakdown, e.g. NVDA A101: 5 edges in run A, only 1 shared with run B). Forcing 'one alpha = one phi' (as C1 does) has already been shown empirically to produce 0% recognition; allowing multiple phi tokens per alpha (one per edge) is the change that makes recognition possible at all on real data.
one_alpha_multiple_phi_tokens_answer.development_plan_support: The Plan's own roadmap language is plural: 'match recurring causal CHAINS [plural] to stable phi-IDs' -- it does not say 'one phi-ID per Alpha'. This is consistent with, not contradicted by, allowing multiple phi tokens per Alpha.

development_plan_alignment: The Plan's own worked example, 'phi-001 = AI demand -> GPU shortage -> NVDA benefits', is itself a 2-hop CHAIN, not a whole-Alpha-graph identity -- textually, the Plan more naturally supports individual recurring causal-chain/motif identities over one monolithic per-Alpha structure identity. However, this audit's own real-data measurement (motif_overlap) shows that EXACT 2-hop chain matching, as literally described in the Plan's example, has ZERO measured cross-run stability today given real independent extraction variance. The recommended edge-level unit (C2, as the base of the C6 hierarchy) is best understood as the Plan's own 'chain' concept truncated to its smallest constituent, unambiguous, currently-stable fragment (a chain of length 1) -- honestly reporting that full multi-hop chain matching, as the Plan envisions it, is not yet achievable without either accepting near-total non-recognition (as measured) or introducing similarity/fuzzy matching (explicitly forbidden by this step's own constraints). The hierarchical structure leaves room to reintroduce a motif layer later if a future step finds a way to close this gap without fuzzy matching (e.g. normalizing edge_type disagreements via an explicit, Product-approved equivalence table -- itself a new PRODUCT_DECISION_REQUIRED, not attempted here).
product_decisions_required: Whether to formally adopt edge-level (C2) as the primary phi matching unit, retaining the current whole-alpha set (C1) only as a secondary aggregate -- this audit recommends it but does not implement it.

Whether an explicit, Product-approved edge_type equivalence/normalization table (e.g. treating 'causal' and 'supportive' as compatible for phi-matching purposes in specific cases) should ever be introduced -- this is a form of controlled, non-fuzzy relaxation distinct from similarity matching, but still a new product decision, not made here.
Whether to keep pursuing motif-level (chain) identity as a stretch goal for a future step given it is empirically unsupported today, or to formally deprioritize it.

Whether alpha-attribution instability (the same edge linked to different alpha_ids across runs) should itself become a tracked, visible phenomenon (e.g. reported as a data-quality signal) -- a new capability, not decided or implemented here.

All Step 1 spec's original open items (ticker-scoping for the other 109 factors, taxonomy-drift migration policy, whether phi ids should be durably persisted) remain equally open and are not resolved by this audit.
